notes: Great-circle distance between CP001's OSM/Nominatim point (26.4494061,56.2027702) and PORT001's OSM/Nominatim locality centroid (23.0046565,70.2162863), computed with the haversine formula on a spherical Earth (R=6371.0088 km). This is the ONLY segment of RT001 with two coordinate-resolvable endpoints: the preceding nodes (SUP001 Saudi Arabia, and the plain-text sea-area labels 'Persian Gulf' and 'Gulf of Oman'/'Arabian Sea') carry no sourced coordinate anywhere in this project's reference data and are skipped, not interpolated. This is a geodesic (straight-line) distance, NOT a navigational/sailing distance - it does not follow any shipping lane, avoid land, or account for the strait's actual navigable channel.

Great-circle distance between CP002 (12.5743764,43.3128158) and PORT006 (12.9298239,74.8224536), haversine on R=6371.0088 km. Preceding nodes (SUP001, export terminal 'Yanbu', and sea-area labels 'Red Sea'/'Gulf of Aden'/'Arabian Sea') have no sourced coordinate and are skipped. Geodesic distance only - does not represent an actual maritime sailing route around the Arabian Peninsula coastline.

Great-circle distance between CP003 (30.6052767,32.3331003) and CP002 (12.5743764,43.3128158), haversine on R=6371.0088 km. This is the Suez-branch alternative of RT004's SUEZ_OR_SUMED branch_group (route_nodes.csv sequence_no 2). A real transit through the Red Sea would follow the Gulf of Suez and Red Sea coastline, not a straight line across the Egyptian and Sudanese landmass; this figure is a geodesic lower bound, not a navigational distance.

Great-circle distance between CP002 (12.5743764,43.3128158) and PORT001 (23.0046565,70.2162863), haversine on R=6371.0088 km. Second leg of the via_suez variant of RT004. Geodesic only, not a sailing distance.

Same geodesic pair as RS004 (CP002 to PORT001); reused here because CP004 SUMED Pipeline - the node this branch actually names in route_nodes.csv - has NULL coordinates (chokepoints.csv: 'Coordinates are null: SUMED is a linear pipeline, not a point feature, and a single centroid would misrepresent it'). CP004 is therefore skipped, not approximated, and this segment represents only the Bab el-Mandeb-to-India maritime leg after the SUMED pipeline's own (unmeasured, in this dataset) length. It is NOT the pipeline's transit distance and must not be read as one.

Great-circle distance between CP006 (-34.3571503,18.4739571) and PORT006 (12.9298239,74.8224536), haversine on R=6371.0088 km. Preceding nodes (SUP006 Nigeria and sea-area labels 'South Atlantic Ocean'/'Indian Ocean'/'Arabian Sea') have no sourced coordinate and are skipped. CP006's coordinate is the OSM Cape of Good Hope headland landmark, not the shipping lane which passes further south (see chokepoints.csv notes) - an additional source of geodesic imprecision beyond the great-circle-vs-sailing-route gap already documented.

Identical geodesic pair and distance to RS006 (CP006 to PORT006) because RT006 and RT007 share the same destination port and the same rounding-the-Cape chokepoint; RT007's own origin (SUP008 Brazil) has no sourced coordinate, so the Brazil-to-Cape leg is not represented here and this figure must not be read as Brazil-to-India distance.
